Definition: of Latin origin; Cyrenius (i.e. Quirinus), a Roman:--Cyrenius.
BiblicalUsage: Quirinius, called Cyrenius in the King James Version, appears once, in the verse that dates the birth of Christ in Luke 2:2. The taxing was first made when he was governor of Syria, and his census brought Joseph and Mary to Bethlehem.
TheologicalSignificance: I take it that the verse is there to anchor the story in history: the Saviour was born under a named governor, in a counted census, in a real year, and the gospel is not a myth.
RelatedPeople: Quirinius; Jesus; Joseph, Husband of Mary
